title: Circuit Judge, 17th Judicial Circuit, Group 52
what_it_does: Circuit judges hear felony criminal cases, major civil suits, family and probate matters. This seat is elected by voters across the 17th Circuit (Broward). Nonpartisan; a candidate needs a majority, and this contest was not decided in August.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); both candidates are marked Qualified, which for a nonpartisan seat means the August vote did not produce a majority winner (or the seat is decided only in November). Positions have not been researched; check the county Supervisor of Elections sample ballot.

candidates.name: David Fry
candidates.background: Fry is a trial attorney who has worked on both sides of criminal cases, serving as an assistant state attorney and as an assistant public defender, and says he has been counsel in more than 70 jury trials across five Florida counties. He also cites experience as trial counsel in complex civil litigation. He led the August 18, 2026 primary for the 17th Circuit Group 52 seat with 33.8% and advanced to the November 3 runoff; the seat is open because Judge Michael G. Kaplan is leaving the bench.

record.item: Says he has served as counsel in more than 70 jury trials in five Florida counties and has worked as both an assistant state attorney and an assistant public defender.

candidates.name: Tamar Hamilton
candidates.occupation: Founder and lead attorney, Law Office of Tamar N. Hamilton, P.A.; adjunct professor, St. Thomas University School of Law
candidates.background: Hamilton runs her own Broward law practice handling civil litigation, real property, probate and contract matters, and has been an adjunct professor at St. Thomas University School of Law since 2018. She was admitted to The Florida Bar in 2014 and is also admitted before the General Legal Council of Jamaica; she earned her J.D. with honors from St. Thomas University School of Law. She has served as a special magistrate, hearing argument and issuing recommended rulings, and advanced to the November 3, 2026 runoff for 17th Circuit Group 52.
